_inherits_note: Intra-family blend: both parents are near_eastern sub-palettes (Persian/axsatran prestige lean + Egyptian/abydosian substrate), so inherits lists near_eastern once.
_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: old_persian (axsatran) backbone + egyptian (abydosian) substrate (Persian-leaning fusion: the satrapal court-tongue over the Nile temple-register)

blend.backbone: old_persian / axsatran register: the satrapal empire-tongue (Xshayathiya/Xshacapavan, vith-houses, Arta the Truth, -aspa/-arta/-farnah/-data endings, the ezafe genitive '-ahya', heavy-syllable stress shifted toward a flowing poetic meter)
blend.overlay: egyptian / abydosian: the Nile (itru) and its inundation, the per-netjer temple and its hem-netjer priesthood, the funerary cult of the justified dead, dj/tj/kh consonants and -aa/-et endings, the per/niut construct toponyms
blend.lean: Persian-heavy - an Achaemenid satrapy-empire planted on the Nile: the Shah crowned as Pharaoh, the rose-court (the paridaida-garden and the apadana-hall) raised over the temple of the river. The Persian rule/kin/court register dominates; the Egyptian substrate endures in the words for the river, the temple, the tomb, and the worked material.

_note: NEW cross-register hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_04 (Achaemenid Persia / Axsatran) x BASE_05 (Ancient Egypt / Abydosian). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: both parents are Civilized (feudal), so Zarkemet is Civilized (feudal). Concept = Achaemenid Egypt: a Persian satrapy-empire on the Nile, the Shah (Xshayathiya) crowned and worshipped as Pharaoh (Per-aa), the satrapal rose-court enthroned over the temple-cities of the river. Backbone/LEAN = Old Persian (the Axsatran satrapal register: the ruling court, the vith-houses, the Arta/Truth ideal, the -aspa/-farnah/-data name-elements); substrate = Egyptian (the Abydosian Nile/temple/funerary register: itru the river, per-netjer the temple, the justified dead, dj/tj/kh phonology). Common-word lexicon is a single FUSED tongue (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md) - Egyptian land/temple/material roots run through Old-Persian phonology, with portmanteaus marking the blended institutions; rank titles use the real Old-Persian/satrapal register (allowed, catalog 5.3) with the Egyptian temple co-titles beneath. DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents - Persian-shifted canon morphs PRIMARY (the Axsatran set: Turvasa, Urlaspa, Gayanta, Naumana, Riyata, Asturna), Egyptian morphs SECONDARY (the Abydosian set), never real Persian/Egyptian gods. Approved foreign display term: the kingdom-tier ruler shows as 'Shah' (the iconic Persian throne; recorded in approved_foreign_terms_used). Religiously TOLERANT in the Axsatran manner: Asturna's peace shelters the Nile cults under the satrapal crown; all three alignments worship (Lawful upholds Arta, Chaotic serves Drauga the Lie). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English (or the approved 'Shah'); conlang titles live in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue.

phonology.palette: Old Persian (axsatran) backbone - vowels a i u with long a/i/u, spirants th(0)/x(kh)/f, sibilants s/sh/z/zh and c(ts), r l, nasals m n, semivowels y v/w, aspirate h; signature endings -a/-ah/-iya/-ana/-aspa/-arta/-farnah/-data and the ezafe genitive '-ahya' - meeting an Egyptian substrate: the dj/tj/kh consonants, the long -aa and feminine -et, the per/niut construct toponyms. Per the CSV: breathy vowels carried on a poetic meter; grammar is VSO with an aspect-based ezafe construction. Theophoric on the Persian-shifted canon morphs (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-, Baga-) with Egyptian temple-variants (Per-, Mery-) beneath.
phonology.phonotactics: CV(C); permitted Persian clusters xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, vr-, thr- absorbing the Egyptian dj/tj/kh as single onsets; vowel length distinctive and breathy; poetic-meter stress (heavy syllables, but softened to a flowing line); the ezafe '-ahya' binds the construct; dithematic Persian court-names over Per-/Niut-/Atash- construct toponyms.

sound_changes: Egyptian dj/tj/kh kept but reshaped to Persian onsets: dj>z/zh, tj>ch/sh, kh>x; the Egyptian glottal weakens to 0
Egyptian endings adapt to the Persian vowel-system: long -aa>-a/-ah, feminine -et>-a/-at, -u>0; roots take a Persian -a/-ah where they would end bare
Old-Persian stress and the ezafe '-ahya' imposed on every root; the breathy long vowels of Egyptian fold into the distinctive Persian a/i/u length, carried on a poetic line
retain the Persian spirants th/x/f and sibilants sh/z/zh and a signature Egyptian dj/tj/kh per word so both ancestries stay audible; very short Egyptian roots take a Persian -a ending
fusion_rules.source_tilt: Egyptian roots for the Nile/temple/funerary/material and staple words (the river-substrate keeps its land: itru, per-netjer, nebu, deshret); Old-Persian roots for rule/kin/court/land/abstract/war words (the satrapal register: pura, puthra, vith, vazraka, aspa); every chosen root is then run through the Persian sound-law so the split is invisible at the surface.

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Egyptian Nile/temple/funerary/material roots + Old-Persian rule/kin/court/land roots, all run through one Old-Persian-shaped sound-law (dj>z/zh, tj>ch/sh, kh>x; Egyptian endings folded into Persian -a/-ah; ezafe-bound, poetic stress); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and the married bloodline. NO slash-pairs - one word per concept.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Persian court-and-satrapal nobility carry a vith-house (vith-X) and a satrapal/court office, with filiation 'X-ahya puthra' (son of X) or compact 'X-puthra'; the Egyptian temple-and-river populace keep the 'sa-' (son of) filiation and theophoric per-constructs; the throne fuses both - a Xshayathiya who is also crowned Per-aa and carries a vith-house over a Per- temple-name.
morphology.compounding_rule: Old-Persian quality/relation + element (Arta-xshaca, truth-realm; Baga-data, god-given), construct via the ezafe '-ahya', layered over Egyptian per/niut construct-chains (Per-[god], Niut-[name]): the capital Zarkemet (Zar- rose/gold + Kemet the black-land), Dida-Itrautah (fort of the river), Per-Turvasa (temple of the sun).

title_ladder.government: feudal (an Old-Persian satrapal court enthroned over the Egyptian temple-cities of the Nile: the Xshayathiya - crowned also as Per-aa - and his vispuhra-kin at the crown, the Xshacapavan-satraps over the nomes, the marzapana-wardens of the marches; the hem-netjer priesthood and the sepati nomarchs serve beneath)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Old-Persian (axsatran) ladder, ascending, with the Egyptian temple-substrate co-titles beneath. Vispati (clan-lord of a vis) barony; Marzapana (march-warden, the marzban) march; Framatar (appointed governor) county over a Parada; Xshacapavan (SATRAP, protector of the realm) duchy over a satrapy (Xshacapavanam); Vispuhra (prince of the blood) principality over a great province (Dahyu); Xshayathiya (king) kingdom over a Xshacam - the kingdom-tier ruler shown by the approved foreign term 'Shah' (the Persian throne), crowned also as Per-aa (Pharaoh) on the Nile; Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings) empire over the Vispa-Dahyu, all the lands. The conquered temple-cities keep their Egyptian sepati (nomarch) and hatia (mayor) and the hem-netjer priesthood beneath the Persian crown; the magi (magu) tend the Atash-fire and the Egyptian wab-priests the river-temple, outside the ladder. Rank titles are the real Old-Persian/satrapal register (allowed); 'Shah' is an approved commonly-known foreign display term.
title_ladder.heir: Mathishta (the greatest; crown prince) / Sa-Nesut (the king's son, in the Egyptian temple-register)

vassalage.vassal: Bandaka (the king's loyal bondsman) / Bak (Egyptian servant)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, except the kingdom-tier ruler which uses the approved foreign term 'Shah' (set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric on the Persian-shifted stems, or an Arta-/Vahu- virtue-name) + filiation (X-puthra); the Persian court-nobility add a vith-house and a satrapal/court office; the Egyptian temple-folk use a theophoric per-name + sa- filiation; order given-first.
surname_source: theophoric given (Baga-data = god-given; Turvasa-data; Egyptian Mery-X)
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Persian court-and-satrapal nobility carry a vith-house and office and Persian-shifted theophorics (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-, Baga-); the Egyptian temple-and-river populace keep theophoric per-names (Mery-X, X-hotep) on the morphed canon-stems with sa- filiation; the throne fuses both - a Persian dithematic court-name crowned as Per-aa.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Persian-register given names from the shifted deity-stems + an Old Persian element: Baga-X (god-X), X-data (X-given), X-farnah (glory-of-X), Vahu-X (good-X), Arta- (Truth); Egyptian-register devotionals: Mery-X (beloved-of-X), X-hotep (X-is-content), Sa-X (son-of-X) on the Egyptian morphs. e.g. Turvasa-data, Baga-Urlaspa, Mery-Tjuraa, Sa-Riaret.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - the Persian-shifted canon morphs PRIMARY (the Axsatran set: Turvasa, Urlaspa, Gayanta, Naumana, Riyata, Asturna, from family_near_eastern via the Old-Persian shift) and the Egyptian morphs SECONDARY (the Abydosian set: Tjuraa, Djeroraa, Riaret, Numenaa), recognizably the same powers, never real Persian/Egyptian gods. Lawful henotheist but TOLERANT in the Axsatran manner: Asturna the Wise Lord Most High upholds ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and the Lawful powers are His yazata-ministers; the Chaotic powers are the hosts of DRAUGA (the Lie). The cardinal sin is the Lie; the Shah's word is bond. The satrapal crown shelters the Nile cults - the per-netjer temples of the river and the funerary cult of the justified dead - under Asturna's peace, never suppressing them. All three alignments worship.
religion.the_one: Asturna (< Aeternus; the Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta and source of the Shah's farnah-glory; in the Egyptian temple-register Atjernaa, the hidden distant maker)

sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gayanta (the enduring earth and the river's-mountain)

sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riyata (the Lady of Waters, mother and mercy; Egyptian Riaret)
sample_deity_renames.Delorum: Djerlaspa (lord of the peaceful dead and the funerary rite; Egyptian Djeroraa)

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Asturna Most High, Turvasa the just sun, Urlaspa of the sworn war, Naumana of the law, Riyata the merciful - upholds ARTA (Truth) against DRAUGA (the Lie), keeps the ever-burning Atash-fire and honors the justified dead of the Nile; names the Chaotic powers the hosts of Drauga, warded
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the honored fore-spirits (the fravashi of the vith-houses and the akhu, the justified dead of the river) and the city-spirits of the per-netjer; the great powers invoked at the fire-altar and the river-temple situationally, as Arta and circumstance require
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon as the hosts of Drauga the Lie made glorious, and names the Lawful powers - and Asturna - as the tyrant-gods of a false order to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers are the hosts of Drauga the Lie, each keeping its morph + a hostile portfolio-epithet (Persian primary, Egyptian secondary): Maraxus -> Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities (Egyptian Marakhu); Vacidus -> Vakida the Devouring-Void (Egyptian Wakedjet the Hefau); Lusanto -> Lusanta the Coin-Serpent (the Lie made gold).

clergy_ladder.5: Magupati (chief magus of a fire-temple) / Hem-netjer Sen-nu (second prophet)
clergy_ladder.7: Dahyu-Magupati (provincial chief magus) / Hem-netjer Tepy (first prophet)
clergy_ladder.9: Magupatan Magupat (chief of chief magi) / Hem-netjer Aa (great prophet)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Atash ([fire] of [power]) and its fire-temple (Atashana) - 'the Atashana of Turvasa' - over the Egyptian Per-netjer (god's-house) of the river - 'the Per-netjer of Tjuraa'; the magi keep the ever-burning fire (Atar), the wab-priests the river-rite.
religion.saints_pattern: the honest dead and the just Shahs kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and petitioned at the fire-altar ('the Arta-true [name]'), alongside the deified justified dead of the Nile (the akhu) honored at the tomb-temple ('the justified [name]', maa-kheru).

holy_symbol_motifs.Asturna: a winged ring-disc (the farnah-glory) above a fire-altar set on the river-bank
holy_symbol_motifs.Turvasa: a rayed sun above the upright Arta-measure and the feather of right-order
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlaspa: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring
